comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete selectors and registry: 130 BDDL tasks, three benchmark files, and two predicate files. All 135 indexed files exist, have unique local paths, and match their manifest SHA-256 values. The registry’s 130 task entries are represented by the BDDL inventory; the complete closest task and Turnon mapping were inspected.
comparisons.objective: The candidate adjusts a gripper opening stop to 90°, locks the coupled screw and jam nut without changing that setting, and verifies retained articulation. LIBERO’s closest task only turns on a stove.
comparisons.physical_skill: The candidate requires coaxial driver and wrench seating, bimanual countertorque, tool withdrawal, and repeated articulated verification. LIBERO requires one stove-control actuation represented by Turnon.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate requires a released opening within ±3°, seated and retained nuts, three repeatable cycles, no more than 2° drift, and hands-off clearance. LIBERO requires only the stove’s boolean turn-on predicate.

closest_tasks.name: turn_on_the_stove
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Actuate the stove control sufficiently to enter its on state.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The Turnon predicate is true; the captured predicate mapping delegates to arg.turn_on().
closest_tasks.reason: It shares rotary actuation but has no adjustable stop, threaded lock, counterholding, setting preservation, or released-cycle verification.

comparisons.reason: Across the complete LIBERO registry, no task tests locking a calibrated screw setting against jam-nut reaction and then verifying retained motion.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete kitchen selectors and inventory: all 381 indexed Python files exist, have unique local paths, and match their manifest hashes. The inventory contains 380 class definitions across atomic and composite tasks. The complete closest intermediate-angular-control definition was inspected.
comparisons.objective: The candidate sets and mechanically locks a gripper’s maximum opening before testing retention. RoboCasa LowerHeat moves a stove knob from high heat into a low-heat interval.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both regulate an articulated angular control, but only the candidate requires concentric two-tool screw/nut engagement and bimanual countertorque that preserves an adjustment during locking.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate grades retained 90° opening, nut seating and retention, three cycles, drift, and release clearance. LowerHeat succeeds whenever the selected stove knob lies in its low-heat interval.

closest_tasks.name: LowerHeat
closest_tasks.objective: Lower a kettle’s heat by adjusting its stove burner knob.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Rotate one stove knob into a permitted angular or state interval.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The target knob’s absolute value must be at least 0.35 and below the suite’s high-heat threshold.
closest_tasks.reason: Intermediate angular regulation overlaps, but LowerHeat does not lock the setting, resist coupled fastener reaction, use concentric tools, or demonstrate retained motion through cycles.

comparisons.reason: The closest RoboCasa task selects an angular range; it does not test mechanically preserving and locking a calibrated stop under countertorque.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified both repository components and all 11 indexed files against their hashes: two SimplerEnv registry/wrapper files and nine ManiSkill environment files. The public registry enumerates 25 task names, and its articulated drawer mappings resolve to captured backend classes. The complete closest drawer implementation, including reset and evaluation, was inspected.
comparisons.objective: The candidate calibrates, locks, and functionally verifies an angular gripper stop. SimplerEnv’s closest task opens a selected cabinet drawer.
comparisons.physical_skill: The candidate requires precision tool seating and coordinated countertorque followed by repeated jaw actuation. OpenDrawer requires pulling one frictional prismatic articulation.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate requires retained angle, locked hardware, repeated cycles, bounded drift, and clearance. OpenDrawer succeeds when drawer qpos reaches at least 0.15.

closest_tasks.name: OpenDrawerInSceneEnv
closest_tasks.objective: Open the selected top, middle, or bottom drawer.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Pull a frictional prismatic drawer joint.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The target drawer joint position is at least 0.15.
closest_tasks.reason: It shares articulated motion only; it lacks fastener adjustment, locking reaction, setting preservation, tools, and post-lock cycle retention.

comparisons.reason: No SimplerEnv registry entry tests threaded adjustment or bimanual locknut counterholding; its closest articulation task measures only drawer displacement.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified both original components and all 1,122 indexed files: 1,018 BEHAVIOR-1K BDDL definitions, 101 legacy BDDL definitions, and three backend Python files. Every file exists, has a unique local path, and matches its hash. The complete furniture and camera definitions and the complete AttachedTo backend were inspected to resolve the abstract attached predicate.
comparisons.objective: The candidate calibrates and locks an adjustable robot-gripper stop and validates retained function. BEHAVIOR’s closest assembly goals attach components or a camera to a supporting structure.
comparisons.physical_skill: The candidate requires driver/wrench seating and countertorque on a coupled screw and jam nut. BEHAVIOR AttachedTo aligns compatible metadata frames after contact and creates a fixed or spherical joint; it does not encode threaded tightening or preservation of a calibrated setting.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate requires a quantitative retained angle, nut retention, three functional cycles, bounded drift, and clearance. BEHAVIOR’s relevant tasks require only named AttachedTo relationships.

closest_tasks.name: attach_a_camera_to_a_tripod
closest_tasks.objective: Attach a digital camera to a camera tripod.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Bring compatible attachment metadata frames into contact and alignment so the backend creates an attachment joint.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The camera’s AttachedTo state names the tripod as its parent.
closest_tasks.reason: A physical tripod may use a screw, but this benchmark’s definition and backend test generic contact-triggered attachment, not threaded engagement, counterholding, calibrated locking, or retained articulation.

closest_tasks.name: assembling_furniture
closest_tasks.objective: Attach a desk bracket to a top and four legs to the bracket.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Align and attach several rigid furniture components through the generic AttachedTo mechanism.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The bracket is attached to the top and every desk leg is attached to the bracket.
closest_tasks.reason: It is multi-component assembly, but its generic attachment predicates do not test adjustment to a numeric setting, locknut reaction, or functional retention cycles.

comparisons.reason: The backend resolves the apparent assembly overlap: the relevant BEHAVIOR tasks create generic metadata-frame attachment joints rather than measuring coupled-fastener calibration and locking.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified both official JSON files against their manifest hashes and inspected the complete catalog scope: 10 published Tier-1 setup/instruction/reset/rubric records and 14 linked procedures. The manifest explicitly identifies only the 10 selected design IDs as benchmark tasks; unselected procedure mappings remain context. The full closest task record was inspected.
comparisons.objective: The candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening stop before verifying retention. DC-knob rotates a marked dimmer knob to a fixed visual mark as a proxy for a UPS rotary-selector operation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require angular alignment to a target. The candidate additionally requires coaxial two-tool seating, countertorque against locknut reaction, regrasping, tool withdrawal, and repeated articulated verification.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate requires ±3° locked retention, three cycles, no more than 2° drift, retained nuts, and one-second clearance. DC-knob gives full credit when the knob line points at the goal mark and partial credit for noticeable clockwise progress.

closest_tasks.name: DC-knob — Turn the knob to the mark
closest_tasks.quote: The line on the knob points at the goal mark (turned clockwise to it).
closest_tasks.objective: Turn a rotary dimmer knob clockwise until its line aligns with the marked goal.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Single-control rotary actuation and visual angular alignment.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Full credit at the goal mark, half credit for noticeable clockwise motion short of it, and zero for no clockwise motion.
closest_tasks.reason: The angular target is a real overlap, but DC-knob has no coupled adjustment screw, jam-nut locking, counterholding, drift constraint, or functional-cycle retention.

comparisons.reason: DataCenterBench contains the strongest target-angle analogue, but its tested outcome is direct selector alignment rather than preserving and locking an adjustable stop under coupled fastener reaction.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete selectors and dynamic registry: 54 task Python files, 55 YAML files, and one registry file. All 110 indexed files exist, have unique paths, and match their hashes; every task module has a same-named YAML configuration, with the additional _task.yml base configuration. The complete fasten_screws implementation and YAML specification were inspected.
comparisons.objective: The candidate adjusts one screw-defined stop, locks the setting with a jam nut, and validates retained gripper motion. RoboDojo fasten_screws inserts and tightens three color-matched screws and nuts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve threaded hardware. The candidate’s essential skill is bimanual counterholding of concentric tools so jam-nut torque does not disturb a calibrated stop; fasten_screws checks alignment and insertion depth for independent fastener pairs.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate requires retained 90° opening, lock seating, repeated cycles, drift limits, and release clearance. fasten_screws scores one, two, or three pairs using upright-axis, 0.001 XY-distance, 0.009 insertion-depth, and open-gripper checks.

closest_tasks.name: fasten_screws
closest_tasks.quote: Insert and tighten each screw into the nut of the same color.
closest_tasks.objective: Insert and tighten each of three screws into the color-matched nut.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Align and seat three independent threaded nut/bolt pairs.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Each credited pair is upright, within 0.001 XY distance, and inserted to the 0.009 depth threshold; grippers must be open.
closest_tasks.reason: This is the closest hardware-level neighbor, but it does not preserve a calibrated setting while tightening a coupled jam nut or verify hands-off retained articulation afterward.

comparisons.reason: Shared tightening does not establish overlap: RoboDojo measures independent fastener insertion and depth, while the candidate measures countertorque-preserved calibration, locking, and functional retention.
